classification.difficultyReason: Find two intercepts and sketch familiar straight lines; variable fractions add arithmetic rather than a new method.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of each line by first finding the $x$- and $y$-intercepts.

answer.worked:
When $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-2x+12\\2x&=12\\x&=6\end{align*}$$
When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-2(0)+12\\y&=12\end{align*}$$
Plot $(6,0)$ and $(0,12)$ and draw the straight line through them.

spec.description: Ungriddded coordinate sketch with labelled intercepts.

$$\begin{align*}0&=-2x+24\\2x&=24\\x&=12\end{align*}$$
When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}3y&=-2(0)+24\\3y&=24\\y&=8\end{align*}$$
Plot $(12,0)$ and $(0,8)$ and draw the straight line through them.

spec.description: Coordinate sketch with both intercepts labelled.

answer.worked:
When $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}6x-3(0)&=18\\6x&=18\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}6(0)-3y&=18\\-3y&=18\\y&=-6\end{align*}$$
Plot $(3,0)$ and $(0,-6)$ and draw the straight line through them.

spec.description: Increasing line through the labelled intercepts.

answer.worked:

When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=0+18\\y&=18\end{align*}$$
Plot $(-18,0)$ and $(0,18)$ and draw the straight line through them.

spec.description: Increasing line crossing the negative x-axis and positive y-axis.

answer.worked:
When $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=2x-11\\2x&=11\\x&=\frac{11}{2}\end{align*}$$
When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=2(0)-11\\y&=-11\end{align*}$$
Plot $\left(\frac{11}{2},0\right)$ and $(0,-11)$ and draw the straight line through them.

spec.description: Increasing line with exact fractional x-intercept.

answer.worked:
When $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}3x-7(0)&=20\\3x&=20\\x&=\frac{20}{3}\end{align*}$$
When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}3(0)-7y&=20\\-7y&=20\\y&=-\frac{20}{7}\end{align*}$$
Plot $\left(\frac{20}{3},0\right)$ and $\left(0,-\frac{20}{7}\right)$ and draw the straight line through them.

spec.description: Increasing line with both fractional intercepts labelled.
